why: Shown reports: MIIT asked both firms for quantities, told firms it intends to approve, and Nvidia aims to ship in late December, before the deadline. Yes forecast follows; reasons hedge correctly; no outside fact.

Only a single-source report of talks plus a possible IPO delay. Nothing shown speaks to talks concluding in a public agreement; Yes within a year is a judgement the evidence neither establishes nor contradicts.

Agreement announced 3 September 2026, about 18 months before the check date; nothing shown reports termination, repricing or delay. Completion forecast follows; answer treats 'acquired' wording as unconfirmed and notes the 'pending' report.

Disclosed maximum guarantee exposure of $105 billion (cap $108.5 billion) plus further credit support and guarantees puts the reported total far above the $25 billion threshold; answer treats caps as ceilings; all figures are in the request.
Shown reports give intent to 'eventually' approve and no approval date; nothing ties approval to before 31 January 2027. Yes is plausible, but the ladder's deadline condition is not evidenced.

Request shows a standing U.S. ban on Nvidia's most advanced chips, easing only for older H200, and no Blackwell authorization signal; RTX Pro 5500 items are China-side. No by deadline follows; reasons consistent, no added facts.

Reported MIIT intent to approve, 'likely to receive approval' and a late-December shipment target support at least one approval by the deadline; rung needs only one purchase. Counter-evidence (H200 precedent, bundling) is weighed; none shows rejection.
Management guides FY2028 gross margin to 72%-73%, midpoint 72.5%, inside rung 3 (71% to below 73%). No shown evidence quantifies a move outside it. Reasons match the request; no added facts.
